- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% gap) with no recent sentiment reversal, consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 2–5% for next period.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags — anticipate upward correction; add 1–3% buffer to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates true price in early days (first 5–7) when sentiment is neutral or negative — apply slight upward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.0/±1.0), model tends to average out — avoid overfitting to recent sentiment; use weighted average of last 5–7 days instead.
